clue.text: Fraud on little woman — man to answer for it

indicators.note: on in a down-to-across sense puts the word for fraud after the other pieces

parts.note: Dot is a pet form of the woman's name Dorothy, and 'little' suits a short name
he is the pronoun for a man
a trick is a deception or fraud

explanation.surface: A swindle on a small woman, and a man must answer for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'answer' is used in its sense of 'serve the purpose'; 'to' and 'for it' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to be effective or suffice, as in 'that will serve'.

clue.text: Plant cut back

definitions.meaning: a coarse weed with broad leaves
to reduce or shorten, as wages or a tail

explanation.definitionFit: The dock is a broad-leaved weed, and to dock pay or a tail is to reduce or shorten it.

clue.text: Leaflets could be loftier

definitions.note: plural clue word for a singular answer: a plant whose leaf has three leaflets

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the next word might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Pamphlets might be more lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaflets' suggests pamphlets, but the answer is a three-leaved plant such as clover.
explanation.definitionFit: A trefoil is a plant like clover whose leaves are made of three leaflets.

clue.text: Surprising gentry with tinier token of affection

indicators.note: surprising suggests the letters are thrown into an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: Upper-class people with a smaller love token would be unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: This band of stones set all round is given as a symbol of enduring love.

clue.text: Benefit entirely absorbed by regular outgoing — that stinks!

definitions.note: an exclamation describing something smelly, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: entirely absorbed by says the benefit word sits completely inside the outgoing word

parts.note: rent is a regular payment going out each month
the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their whole benefit is swallowed by rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The DOLE is British unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means smelling strongly of something, so a thing that stinks is this.

clue.text: Mothball used where larva is found

definitions.meaning: to preserve something (such as a ship) unused by sealing it
the silky case spun by a larva before it becomes an adult

explanation.definitionFit: To mothball equipment is to seal it in protective covering, and a pupating larva lives inside a silk case.

clue.text: Rocks make voyage change direction

indicators.note: change direction tells us to turn the voyage word round, reading it right to left

parts.note: to sail is to make a voyage

explanation.surface: Instructions for a ship to alter course among dangerous rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change direction' turns SAIL into LIAS. The Lias is a series of Lower Jurassic rock strata in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lias is a geological formation of limestone and shale beds, i.e. rocks.

clue.text: 'Criminal!'. I shall say, 'Gangster!

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
say, as in for example, is EG
Al Capone, the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a gangster is a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: AL comes from Al Capone, the Prohibition-era gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something against the law, unlawful.

clue.text: Mr. Grimes and his like conduct a lottery

parts.note: Mr Grimes is the chimney sweep in Kingsley's The Water-Babies; his like are chimney sweeps
to take someone somewhere is to conduct them

explanation.surface: Grimes and people like him run a raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a gamble in which the stakes go to the winners, a kind of lottery.

clue.text: English composer replaces nothing in hit — he's a know-all

indicators.note: replaces says the composer letters take the place of the nothing letter in the word for hit

parts.note: to clock someone is slang for hitting them
O looks like zero, nothing
Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A British composer substitutes for a blank in a hit record, by a smart alec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English composer' is not one English composer but E plus VERDI, put in place of the O of CLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is British slang for a smug person who thinks he knows everything.

clue.text: Fellow takes shelter in Levant

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A man seeks refuge in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Levant' looks like the region, but here it is the old verb 'to levant', to run away (especially leaving debts unpaid).
explanation.definitionFit: To levant is an old word for absconding or running off.

clue.text: Sorry girl's given the job

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, with 's as a possessive
appointed means given a post

explanation.surface: A woman is apologetic on being hired.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorry in the sense of let down or saddened by an outcome.

clue.text: Continue being a fool

explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to carry on, and a goon is a silly or stupid person.

clue.text: Searching the dictionary for 'on the mend'

definitions.meaning: consulting a reference book for a word

explanation.definitionFit: One consults a reference book for a word this way, and things improving are said to be doing this too.

clue.text: Put out, group leader organises an attack

indicators.note: put out suggests something knocked out of place, so letters are rearranged
leader is the first letter of the word group

explanation.surface: Annoyed, the head of a group arranges an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed' but it signals the anagram of G plus ORGANISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggression is hostile behaviour or an unprovoked assault.

clue.text: It helps in setting a leg that's broken; can end in cure

indicators.note: a broken leg is in pieces, so the letters of these two words are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
a tin is a can

indicators.note: end in picks out the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Advice on putting a fractured leg in plaster, with a hint at curing.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface misleads: 'setting' is jelly setting, not a bone. 'broken' rearranges A LEG into GELA; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooks add this protein to make jellies and desserts set firm.

clue.text: Village hero

definitions.meaning: the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy, its protagonist

explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village, and Hamlet is the protagonist of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Left in poor health, I acquire place in the country

parts.note: ill means unwell
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A sick person moves to a rural home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquire' and 'in' are link words. The country is the land of tiny people in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput is the fictional land of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels, a nation.

clue.text: Recompense the artist Turner

indicators.note: Turner here means something that turns, so the artist's word is turned backwards

parts.note: an artist who draws is a drawer

explanation.surface: Paying J.M.W. Turner, the English landscape painter, for his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J.M.W. Turner but is the reversal signal: DRAWER turned is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean payment or compensation given for a service.

clue.text: Court — girl turned up in a sweater

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: turned up means flipped upward, so in a down clue the girl's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Nell is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman being courted appears wearing a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted garment made of sheep's wool is a woolly jumper.

clue.text: Fix puncture — a minor irritation

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
a prick is a small puncture

explanation.surface: Mending a flat tyre is a small nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny hole made by a needle point stands figuratively for a petty annoyance.

clue.text: Make cross part of religious ceremonial

definitions.meaning: perfumed smoke burnt in church rites

explanation.definitionFit: To anger greatly, and also fragrant smoke burnt in worship.

clue.text: Wrap novel concerning love

parts.note: Kim is Kipling's novel
on means about or concerning
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A book about love is given as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an anagram signal but is Kipling's book KIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose Japanese robe that wraps around the body.

clue.text: Bird seen to behave amorously more than once

parts.note: to spoon is old slang for kissing and cuddling
to bill (as in 'bill and coo') is to behave lovingly

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted courting repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' tells us to use 'behave amorously' twice, giving two different synonyms; 'seen to' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird is named for its long flat bill with a broad tip.

clue.text: Old-fashioned American muffin — cake-like, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An American baked goods item is described as quaint and rather cake-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were an ancient people of South America, so one is an American of long ago.

clue.text: Birds think out loud

indicators.note: out loud says the word for think is spoken, giving letters that sound alike

parts.note: to muse is to ponder

explanation.surface: Birds are said to ponder audibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mews are gulls, an old plural of the seabird name mew.

clue.text: I don't like your leads, but in vain

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters, the ones at the front

explanation.surface: Someone tells a dog walker, or actor, they dislike their leads, to no avail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is taken as it stands; 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to no purpose or futilely is doing it this way, an adverb matching 'in vain'.

clue.text: Rival good, but short of one skill

parts.note: to rival is to compete

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is removed from the word for good

parts.note: nice means good
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rival is good but lacks one ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of one' removes I from NICE, leaving NCE; 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability or proficiency to do a job is synonymous with skill.

clue.text: Not a single sister, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for sister is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a nun is a sister in a religious order

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have no sister at all, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not even one, no single person or thing.

clue.text: Pong is softened, modified

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad smell has been reduced and adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: PONG is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A pong is a stink, and stinkingness is the quality of foul smell.
